title: eng-hiring-onboarding-interview-debriefs-weekly-sync-2026-03-17
content:
Weekly hiring/onboarding sync - notes and action items
Date: 2026-03-16
Attendees: Priya (owner), Alex, Jordan, Samira, Taylor (hiring partner) - quick drop-in from People Ops
Goal: sync on active pipeline, share interview debriefs, identify blockers for onboarding new hires, check team health indicators

1) Quick pipeline snapshot
- Open reqs: 5 (2 backend/platform eng, 1 infra reliability, 1 applied-ml infra, 1 full-stack infra tools)
- Candidates in loop: ~12 (5 on-site / onscreen final stage, 4 take-home/code challenge, 3 phone screens)
- Hiring velocity: slow last 2 weeks due to interviewer availability + overloaded sprint cycles
- Priority: fill 2 platform-engineering IC3/IC4 roles (productivity and runtime) ASAP

2) Interview debriefs (this week)
- Candidate A (Backend/Runtime) - onsite 2026-03-14
  - Positive: deep systems design, previous experience shipping GPU inference infra, strong perf debugging stories
  - Concerns: limited familiarity with our specific runtime optimizations (kv cache/continuous batching) but quick learner
  - Score: hire-with-caveat (recommendation: follow-up take-home on batching design + a 1:1 pairing session with runtime lead)
  - Action: Alex to schedule pairing week of 3/22; Priya to request final reference check

- Candidate B (Infra Reliability) - onscreen 2026-03-15
  - Positive: incident postmortem discipline, SLO-driven signal design, solid on runbooks and oncall automation
  - Concerns: limited experience with GPU resource scheduling (mostly CPU infra)
  - Outcome: move to final with hiring manager prep; ask scenario about degraded GPU pool recovery
  - Action: Jordan to draft scenario prompt and send to candidate before final loop

- Candidate C (Applied ML infra) - take-home submitted 2026-03-13
  - Positive: strong infra-ML tooling experience, nice reproducible evaluation harness in repo
  - Concerns: code quality needs cleanup; tests lacking for edge cases
  - Outcome: invite to code-walkthrough; Samira to lead walkthrough session

3) Onboarding status (new hires in last 60 days)
- New hire: Maya (SRE) - week 5
  - Progress: completed infra runbooks, shadowed oncall twice, started first small pager triage task
  - Blockers: no access to internal GPU telemetry dashboard (ticket raised to infra tooling: TOOLS-112)
  - Action: Samira follow-up with infra-tools owner, escalate if not resolved by 3/19

- New hire: Carlos (Platform eng IC3) - week 2
  - Progress: did init repo walk, completed first small bug fix, onboarding buddy assigned (Jordan)
  - Blockers: onboarding schedule overloaded - many required meetings scheduled in same block; reduce meeting load next week to allow focused pairing
  - Action: Jordan to propose a lighter schedule for week 3

4) Team health signals / notes
- Morale: mixed - recent load from oncall and hiring cadence causing context switching. Several engineers (notably runtime) pushing overtime to help interviews + product deadlines.
- Retention risk: medium for a couple of IC4s (expressed interest in less context switching); recommend manager 1:1s to discuss growth and focused scope.
- Burn indicators: increased number of mentions in Slack of late-syncs, fewer PR reviewers available -> backlog of reviews growing (avg PR review time +48h)
- Suggestion: temporary review rotation to clear review queue; ask PMs to freeze non-critical scope for 1 sprint for key teams (runtime, infra)

5) Blockers across hiring/onboarding
- Interviewer bandwidth: many interviewers are oncall/sprints; need to protect slots for final loops to keep candidates moving
- Access issues for hires (dashboards, repos, svc accounts) - multiple tickets opened; onboarding owner to triage weekly
- Offer timeline friction: compensation approvals taking 5-7 business days; lost candidate last week for competing offer. People Ops to propose fast-track approval for critical roles

6) Decisions / proposals
- Fast-track offers for priority roles (2 platform-engineering reqs) - agreed in principle. People Ops (Taylor) to propose approval workflow by 3/19.
- Reduce meeting load for new hires first 2 weeks - adopt a "quiet onboarding" template for next cohort. Jordan to draft template by 3/20.
- Temporary code review rotation for 2 weeks focused on runtime and infra; volunteers: Alex, Jordan, Priya, Samira - rotation start 3/18.

7) Action items (owner, due)
- Alex: schedule pairing session with Candidate A and runtime lead; due 2026-03-22
- Priya: request final reference check for Candidate A; due 2026-03-18
- Jordan: draft GPU recovery scenario for Candidate B and send; due 2026-03-19
- Samira: lead code-walkthrough for Candidate C; schedule with candidate; due 2026-03-20
- Samira: follow-up on Maya's telemetry access ticket TOOLS-112; due 2026-03-19
- Taylor (People Ops): propose fast-track approval workflow for offers for priority roles; due 2026-03-19
- Jordan: draft "quiet onboarding" schedule template; due 2026-03-20
- All: volunteer for code review rotation (confirm availability in #eng-hiring on Slack); due 2026-03-17

8) Notes to hiring managers
- Keep final loop interviewers protected from high-priority sprint tasks where possible - we are losing candidates to delays.
- For candidates with strong systems knowledge but lacking specific runtime experience, consider pairing projects as part of ramp plan (fast way to assess ability + reduces rejection false negatives).

9) Misc
- Headcount update: finance signaled green light for +3 hires in Q2 for platform and infra teams - still waiting on exact budget SKU. Priya to sync with finance 3/18.
- Next sync: weekly on Mondays 10:00am PT - next meeting 2026-03-23 (tentative)

End of notes.
